newsitem.title: USA: U.S. warns against travel in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: U.S. warns against travel in Zaire.

text.p: The United States on Saturday warned U.S. citizens against travelling in eastern Zaire, saying the security situation was "deteriorating" as conflict between Tutsi rebels and Zairean troops threatened to spread.

"Recent visits to this area by U.S. embassy officers have met with security incidents," the State Department said. "Security and logistical support provided by even experienced international organisations are not exempt from the risk."
The travel warning covered the Kivu regions, both north and south, including the cities of Goma, Bukavu and Uvira.
"The security situation in both north and south Kivu continues to deteriorate and there is now active fighting in the region," the department said in a written statement.

Inter-ethnic violence was no longer controlled in Zaire's Masisi region, nor along major roads near refugee camps, but had spilled over into other regions "including the subzones which border Uganda," it said.
"Given the unsettled situation and the unpredictability of events, American citizens should avoid all travel there."

The rebels were reported on Saturday to have captured two towns in the east of the country, to have frightened 200,000 Rwandans into fleeing the second biggest refugee camp in Zaire and to have wounded 50.
A string of camps in Zaire houses 1.1. million Rwandan refugees, including perpetrators of the 1994 genocide in Rwanda in which Hutus killed up to one million Tutsis and moderate Hutus.
In total, nearly half-a-million refugees are now estimated to be on the move as a result of Tutsi rebel tactics.
Both Rwanda and Burundi, Zaire's small neighbours to the east, are governed by Tutsi ethnic minorities and diplomats fear they could be drawn into the conflict.
